scope: D2PRL GPU convolution owned readback, tested independently of the full learned model and 96 MP workload.

change.output: The mapped staging view is returned with release(); no Float32Array.slice or equivalent output backing copy.
change.ownership: release unmaps/destroys and releases the reservation exactly once. Engine disposal defers device destruction until every returned result is released. Input and intermediate GPU buffers are destroyed before mapping recovery.
change.budget: Two output extents cover staging plus a separate host mapping. Initial total reservation is unchanged; no global resource ceiling is reduced.
change.transferContract: Mapped WebGPU ArrayBuffers are not transferable. Current D2PRL callers consume these views synchronously or await downstream useful copying before releasing them; progress callbacks expose no mapped buffers.

coverage: two outstanding outputs and mapped input to a later convolution
mapping plus range refusal retry one completed dispatch only
cancellation after mapping releases unpublished output

resourceOpportunityIntegration.scope: Resource-owner and backing-release hooks only; the already qualified GPU arithmetic and mapped-output contract are unchanged.
coverage: waits for real independent useful work after insufficient reclaim without another allocation attempt
GPU retirement cannot wake an ArrayBuffer-domain wait
exact ArrayBuffer retirement permits the suspended useful operation to resume
worker scheduler forwards the D2PRL owner so its own concurrent lanes do not count as independent producers
mapped output emits GPU retirement only and still releases idempotently
resourceOpportunityIntegration.backingDomain: GPU buffer destruction reports gpu only. A host-visible WebGPU mapped view is not evidence that its backing belongs to Chromium's ordinary ArrayBuffer allocator.
